column1: # class-overrides.tsv — per-class runner accommodations for run-hib.sh
# THIS FILE IS TRACKED IN GIT ON PURPOSE.
# `apps/` is gitignored wholesale (.gitignore:12), so everything else in
# apps/hib-suite-runner/ carries no history: it cannot be diffed, blamed, or
# restored, and it has already been silently lost twice —
#   * 2026-07-16: the driver files (rerun.sh, common.args, CratonRunner.java,
#     testlist.txt, ...) were truncated to zero bytes by local disk exhaustion
#     and were restored from a hib-suite-runner.tar backup three weeks stale;
#   * 2026-07-22 -> 2026-07-31: the per-class timeout/mode accommodation for
#     DefaultCatalogAndSchemaTest was implemented, validated, documented as
#     "Resolved", and then vanished from run-hib.sh with nothing to flag it.
#     See docs/known-issues/... (now fixed-suite-bugs/hibernate/
#     qualfiedtablenaming-runner-timeout-floor-lost-20260731-FIXED.md).
# run-hib.sh and this table are force-added (`git add -f`) past the apps/
# ignore so a future truncation or stale-backup restore shows up as a normal
# `git status` modification instead of disappearing invisibly.
# FORMAT — tab-separated, three columns. `#` comments and blank lines ignored.
#   <fully.qualified.TestClass>   <timeout-seconds | ->   <extra VM flags | ->
#   timeout   a FLOOR, not an absolute: the class runs with
#             max(this, the run's --timeout/$TIMEOUT). `-` = no override.
#   flags     extra CratonVM flags appended for this class only, before the
#             @common.args argfile. Space-separated. Already-present flags are
#             not duplicated. `-` = none.
# Verify the table is actually live before trusting a suite run:
#     ./run-hib.sh overrides
# A run whose header does not print `overrides=N (loaded)` is running without
# these accommodations and will misreport the classes below.
# DefaultCatalogAndSchemaTest — 132-method @ParameterizedClass matrix, each
# method bootstrapping a SessionFactory and generating DDL. Legitimately far
# slower than the suite's flat 300s per-class cap, so it needs a floor; without
# one `timeout` kills it at 300s and it is reported HANG with ms=0 and no
# @@RESULT, forever. Root cause of the original hang: fixed-suite-bugs/
# hibernate/qualfiedtablenaming-hang-cluster-20260721-FIXED.md
# THE OLD RATIONALE HERE WAS STALE, AND SO WERE ITS NUMBERS. It said the class
# was "deliberately quarantined to the interpreter (41cdfdf94)" via
# NamingHelper.hashedName -> BigInteger.toString(35) ->
# java/math/MutableBigInteger, and quoted clean runtimes of 620,902-1,804,813
# ms. That quarantine was REMOVED on 2026-07-31 with the last static ban mirrors
# (see the #[ignore] on `hibernate_biginteger_divide_cluster_is_never_background_enqueued`
# in jit/src/tiered.rs) — the comment outlived the defect by six weeks and would
# have sent the next reader hunting a JIT ban that no longer exists.
# What the time actually was, measured 2026-08-11 on Azure Linux with
# `perf record`: `Arena::alloc` at 76% of all CPU, i.e. the arena span tier's
# unbounded first-fit scan (fixed by keying it on size, gc/src/arena.rs). JIT-ON
# was 3.8x SLOWER than --nojit before that fix and is faster than it after.
# Sequential, same box, same 1500m heap, 132/132 both sides:
#   real HotSpot   30s
#   CratonVM      516s   (was ~2300s)
# Still 17x, hence the floor stays — but 3600s is now generous rather than
# barely sufficient, and a full-suite shard run measured 2194s under six-way
# contention, so do not lower it without re-measuring under load.
org.hibernate.orm.test.boot.database.qualfiedTableNaming.DefaultCatalogAndSchemaTest
# OffsetDateTimeTest / ZonedDateTimeTest — legitimately slow, not a hang.
# Both were originally read as witnesses of the moving-young-inert-under-JIT
# throughput tax
# (docs/known-issues/hibernate/moving-young-inert-under-jit-throughput-tax-20260730.md).
# That is Generational-collector reasoning and the default collector moved to
# ZGC on 2026-08-10; the cost under the CURRENT default was measured directly
# on 2026-08-11 with `perf record`, and it was the ZGC conservative-root
# interior-pointer walk (80.7% of all CPU samples in `VmHeap::is_heap_addr`),
# fixed by the backwards object-start bit scan in `gc/src/zgc.rs`. Post-fix,
# ZonedDateTimeTest runs found=608 ok=404 failed=0 aborted=204 in 381s on Azure
# Linux at --Xmx 1500m — byte-identical counts to real HotSpot, which takes
# 17s. So: still 20x+ HotSpot, still well over the suite's flat 300s cap, and
# still not a hang. Not the same defect as DefaultCatalogAndSchemaTest above —
# this is throughput, not correctness — but the mechanism (a flat cap too tight
# for a legitimately slow class) is identical, so the same floor applies.
org.hibernate.orm.test.type.temporal.OffsetDateTimeTest
org.hibernate.orm.test.type.temporal.ZonedDateTimeTest
# SmokeTests — same shape, arrived at from the opposite direction. Until
# 2026-08-11 this class did not reach its own timeout at all: it died with
# `OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space` allocating ANTLR's `DFAState[8192]`
# (65552 bytes) into a free list holding 1.13 GiB whose largest hole was 65528
# bytes — the ZGC TLAB chunk size, which on a non-compacting heap is the
# granularity of free-list holes (fixed by raising ZGC_TLAB_MAX_CHUNK to
# 512 KiB; see gc/src/zgc.rs). With that gone it is merely slow: found=17
# ok=16 failed=0 skipped=1 in 322s at --Xmx 1500m, matching real HotSpot's
# counts exactly (HotSpot: 10s). 322s is just past the flat 300s cap, and the
# margin closes further under host load, so it needs the same floor as the
# temporal pair rather than a 10% one.
org.hibernate.orm.test.sql.exec.SmokeTests
# ASTParserLoadingTest — the one entry here whose slowness is NOT the VM's.
# It is the class whose 300s kill caused the cross-class stale-schema cascade
# (fixed-suite-bugs/hibernate/mysql-cross-class-stale-schema-shared-worker-db-
# 20260822.md): killed at the cap, it left its 54 tables behind for every later
# class on the shard that shares a table name. The harness now resets a shard's
# worker database after a kill, so the cascade is closed either way — but with
# no floor the class is still reported HANG with no per-test breakdown, which is
# exactly how its supposed "21 real failures" stayed unexamined for a week.
# MEASURED 2026-08-27, one fresh MySQL 8.0.46 database per arm, same box, same
# common.args, serial on an idle machine:
#   real HotSpot 25.0.3+9   104 ok, 0 failed   502s
#   CratonVM (ZGC, 1500m)   104 ok, 0 failed   633s     <- 1.26x, not 25x
# HotSpot is over the cap too, which is the whole point: the wall is the
# DATABASE, not the VM. Both arms issue a byte-identical 8533 SQL statements,
# of which 6495 (76%) are DDL — 5616 `truncate table` alone, i.e. the fixture
# truncating its ~54 tables after each of 104 tests. On InnoDB a TRUNCATE is a
# tablespace drop-and-recreate, and that is what the 500-600s is.
# The floor is 3600 rather than ~1200 because the wall scales with load on the
# DATABASE, not on the CPU: six concurrent copies (one fresh schema each, as a
# six-way shard run would produce) took 1452-1456s each. That is also where the
# page's headline "1447s" came from.
org.hibernate.orm.test.hql.ASTParserLoadingTest
